gi16_aid.topic: US military aid to Israel: the 2016 MOU, emergency aid since Oct 2023, shares of budget and GDP, and the fungibility test

claims.text: CRS: 2016 MOU signed 14 Sept 2016 for FY2019–2028, $38bn: $33bn FMF grants plus $5bn missile defence; both sides commit 'not to seek changes to the FMF levels for the duration of this understanding'; MOU runs through 30 Sept 2028
CRS: total US aid obligations to Israel 1946–2025 about $174bn current dollars; about $298bn in constant 2024 dollars for 1946–2024

CRS: the 2007 MOU allowed up to 26.3% of aid to be spent on Israeli-made equipment (offshore procurement); under the 2016 MOU OSP decreases slowly until FY2024 then phases out more sharply, 'ending entirely in FY2028'

CRS: since FY1991 Congress has required Israel's FMF to be disbursed as a lump sum in the first month of the fiscal year, into an interest-bearing account at the Federal Reserve Bank; annual FMF grants are 'approximately 14%' of Israel's overall defence budget; Israel's defence spending 8.8% of GDP in 2024

CRS on P.L. 118-50 (April 2024): FMF $3.5bn (of which $769.3m or more may be spent on Israeli equipment), missile defence $4bn, Iron Beam $1.2bn; two US-owned Iron Dome batteries transferred 24 Oct 2023; Aug 2024 notifications >$20bn incl. F-15IA $18.82bn; Jan 2025 Trump released hold on 1,800 MK-84 bombs; 28 Feb 2025 emergency declaration ~$4bn; Rubio said it 'reverse[d] the Biden Administration's partial arms embargo'; Israel's Defence Ministry (27 May 2025): more than 90,000 tons of armaments on 800 planes and 140 ships

INSS (Feb 2026): US military aid has fallen to 'about half a percent' of Israeli GDP and is 'roughly 15%' of Israel's defence budget; the option to convert aid to shekels for domestic procurement has been eroded and will disappear by 2028, so aid goes almost exclusively to procurement in the US; recommends a gradual move to a business partnership, not dollar-for-dollar replacement

Bandow (Cato, 2012) citing Israeli economist Gazit: in 2011 US aid was 1.5% of Israel's GDP, 4% of the government budget and 24% of security outlays; three-quarters of the $3bn had to buy US weapons, a hidden cost Gazit put at about $600m, 'a fifth of the nominal' aid; Bandow: 'money is fungible' (applied to Egypt and Jordan aid)

National Interest (June 2016): 'Money is fungible'; OSP of $815m, just over 26% of the package, lets Israel 'divert funds from its defense-technology accounts' to settlements; estimated settlement spending at least $250m a year (uncertain, spread across accounts); proposed withholding OSP tied to settlement spending

Loan guarantees (CRS data via JVL): the 1992 $10bn guarantees (P.L. 102-391) could be reduced by an amount equal to Israel's settlement expenditures; reductions 1994–97 totalled $1,358.8m, less $585m reinstated for security, net $773.8m; under the 2003 $9bn guarantees reductions of $289.5m (2003) and $795.8m (2005)

Bank of Israel: defence expenditure 5.3% of GDP (2015–19 avg), 4.2% (2022), 5.2% (2023), 8.4% (2024), 7.8% (2025), ~5.5% projected 2026–30; gross war cost NIS 34bn (2023), 133bn (2024), 116bn (2025), 69bn projected (2026), total NIS 352bn ('approximately NIS 350 billion'), excluding decisions after late Feb 2026; special US grant NIS 13bn (2023), 6bn (2024), 6bn (2025), total NIS 25bn; gross public debt 61.3% (2023), 67.6% (2024), 68.5% (2025) of GDP

Knesset passed the 2026 budget 30 March 2026, 62-55; defence budget about $44.8bn, about $9.48bn more than previous year; record $268bn total; Bismuth: 'approximately ₪22 billion' of it is 'expenditure contingent on income, including the U.S. aid grant and other revenues'

Next MOU: Axios (Nov 2025) reported Israel sought a 20-year deal shifting toward joint R&D; Netanyahu (Jan 2026) called for winding down aid over a decade; in a 1 June 2026 letter to Rep. Stutzman: 'The time has now arrived for us to move from aid recipient to partner'; Huckabee: 'New MOU w/ Israel ends aid & will be based on trade'; joint statement aim 'gradually transition from aid to a completely reciprocal partnership'; formal talks began week of 1 June 2026

Netanyahu, CNBC interview (June 2026): 'I want it to start now, I want it to start in the last two years of the Trump administration', until aid reaches 'coming to zero'; Trump was initially not supportive when Netanyahu raised it in late December

claims.text: Israel Finance Ministry preliminary estimate (12 April 2026): the 2026 war with Iran cost NIS 35bn ($11.52bn) in budgetary expenses, NIS 22bn of it defence; already added to the 2026 budget

Bank of Israel: June 2025 Iran operation not costed separately; about NIS 4bn (later about NIS 6bn) Property Tax Fund compensation for its damage; NIS 31bn addition to the 2025 budget financed it and the Gaza fighting; 2025 central government deficit about NIS 99bn, 4.7% of GDP; 2024 6.7%

gi16_americans.topic: US service members and American civilians killed in the theatres of the wars since Oct 2023, and earlier context

claims.text: 11 Jan 2024, off Somalia: Navy Special Warfare Operators Christopher J. Chambers and Nathan G. Ingram lost while boarding an 'illicit dhow carrying Iranian advanced conventional weapons' (Houthi missile components) in rough seas; one knocked off by waves, a teammate went in after him; declared deceased 21 Jan 2024

Sgt Quandarius Stanley, 23, Army motor transport operator, 7th Transportation Brigade (Expeditionary), critically injured in May 2024 when high winds and heavy seas damaged the Gaza pier; officials said not combat-related; died in late Oct/early Nov 2024 (reported 5 Nov 2024)

Iran war: Sgt Michael Emmanuel Swinton, 30, Army, 'killed in action' 19 July 2026 at Erbil Air Base, Iraq; Oct 9 DCAS update raised toll to 21 by adding Maj. Sorffly Davius (NY Army National Guard, died 6 March at Camp Buehring, Kuwait, medical emergency) and an unnamed Navy enlisted woman (September, non-hostile, cause pending); 865 wounded since 28 Feb, majority after 7 July; WaPo had reported four more deaths than the count; Hegseth disputed; an official said the additional deaths 'were not directly related to the war with Iran'

Newsweek (23 Sept 2026): 19th death Capt. Bianca C. Wilkerson, 37, US Army Central, died 18 Sept 2026 in Qatar in a 'non-combat related incident'; earlier deaths included a Navy officer in a helicopter crash, six airmen in a KC-135 crash, three soldiers killed in Jordan after attacks on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base when fighting resumed in July (Sgt Angel Rampersad 'killed in action on July 17'), and a soldier who died in Iraq while troops tried to disable a crashed Iranian drone; DCAS then listed 19 deaths and more than 820 wounded

Sayfollah 'Saif' Musallet, 20, of Tampa, Florida, killed 11 July 2025 in Sinjil; family and Palestinian Health Ministry: beaten to death by Israeli settlers, ambulance blocked; IDF: rocks thrown at settlers led to a violent confrontation, examined by ISA and police; State Department confirmed a US citizen's death; ABC lists earlier US citizens killed in the West Bank since 7 Oct 2023: Tawfic Abdel Jabbar, 17 (19 Jan 2024), Mohammad Alkhdour, 17 (10 Feb 2024), Aysenur Eygi, 26 (6 Sept 2024), Amer Rabee, 14 (6 April 2025)

Aysenur Eygi, 26, US and Turkish citizen, shot in the head at a protest in Beita on 6 Sept 2024; IDF: 'highly likely' hit 'indirectly and unintentionally' by IDF fire aimed at 'the key instigator of the riot'; Biden 'outraged', called for 'full accountability'; Blinken: 'unprovoked and unjustified'

Tawfic Abdel Jabbar, 17, of Gretna, Louisiana, killed 19 Jan 2024 on Highway 60 near al-Mazra'a ash-Sharqiya; Israeli police said an off-duty police officer, an IDF soldier and a settler opened fire; police and IDF said he threw rocks, disputed by a passenger, his father and B'Tselem; Kirby: 'a tragic killing'; no findings released or charges by July 2025

Amer Rabee, 14, of Saddle Brook, New Jersey, killed near Turmus Ayya (April 2025); IDF said it identified 'three terrorists who hurled rocks toward the highway'; community centre said he was shot 11 times; State Department said Israel is 'investigating'

Rachel Corrie, 23, killed 16 March 2003 in Rafah by an armoured Israeli bulldozer while trying to stop a home demolition; operator said he did not see her; Israel's Supreme Court (12 Feb 2015) upheld the 2012 Haifa District Court ruling, exempting the state under the 'wartime activity' exception; HRW: the ruling 'sends a message that Israeli forces have immunity even for deaths caused by alleged negligence'
Blinken told the UN on 24 Oct 2023 that 33 Americans were killed in the 7 October attack; a State Department official said 10 were unaccounted for and may be held hostage

1 April 2024 WCK strikes in Gaza killed seven aid workers incl. Jacob Flickinger (American-Canadian dual national); IDF FFAM: 'a grave mistake', misidentification and breaches of rules of engagement; two officers dismissed, three reprimanded; MAG considering further action (Binskin report, 2 Aug 2024)

Wikipedia (Killing of Tawfic Abdel Jabbar), as of March 2026: no criminal charges had been brought in killings of Americans by Israelis since January 2022; Biden's Feb 2024 executive order sanctioning settlers responded to settler violence including this killing and was repealed by Trump in Jan 2025
